passages.text: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the teacher and leader.
Jesus had twelve disciples.
Jesus finished giving instructions to His twelve disciples.
After this, Jesus left that place.
Jesus went to the cities of His disciples.
Jesus taught in those cities.
Jesus preached in those cities.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων τοῖς δώδεκα μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ μετέβη ἐκεῖθεν τοῦ διδάσκειν καὶ κηρύσσειν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν αὐτῶν

passages.text: Meanwhile John heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent his disciples to ask Him, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
passages.sermon:
John was in prison.
John heard about the works of Christ.
John sent his disciples to Jesus.
John told his disciples to ask Jesus a question.
John’s disciples asked Jesus, “Are you the One who was to come?”
They also asked, “Should we look for someone else?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης ἀκούσας ἐν τῷ δεσμωτηρίῳ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Χριστοῦ πέμψας διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Go back and report to John what you hear and see: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the disciples of John.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “Go back to John.
Tell him what you hear.
Tell him what you see.
Blind people receive their sight.
Lame people walk.
People with leprosy are cleansed.
Deaf people hear.
Dead people are raised.
The poor hear the good news.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν καὶ χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται

passages.text: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, “Blessed is the person who does not fall away because of Me.”
passages.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί

passages.text: As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw John’s disciples leaving.
Jesus began to speak to the crowds.
Jesus spoke about John the Baptist.
Jesus asked the crowds a question.
He said, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see?”
He asked, “Did you go to see a reed swaying in the wind?”
passages.original: Τούτων δὲ πορευομένων ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγειν τοῖς ὄχλοις περὶ Ἰωάννου Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον

passages.text: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds about John the Baptist.
He asked them a question.
He said, "What did you go out to see?"
He asked, "Did you go to see a man wearing fine clothes?"
He explained, "People who wear fine clothes live in kings’ palaces."
John the Baptist did not wear fine clothes.
John the Baptist did not live in a palace.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἠμφιεσμένον ἰδοὺ οἱ τὰ μαλακὰ φοροῦντες ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις τῶν βασιλέων εἰσίν

passages.text: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds about John the Baptist.
He asked them a question.
He said, "What did you go out to see?"
He asked, "Did you go to see a prophet?"
He answered, "Yes, I tell you, you saw a prophet."
He said, "John is more than a prophet."
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε προφήτην ἰδεῖν ναί λέγω ὑμῖν καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου

passages.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist is the person spoken about in Scripture.
God said these words about him.
God said, “Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you.”
This messenger will go before you.
He will prepare your way before you.”
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου Ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου

passages.text: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “I tell you the truth.”
No one born of a woman is greater than John the Baptist.
John the Baptist is the greatest among all people born naturally.
But the least person in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John the Baptist.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐκ ἐγήγερται ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν μείζων Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it.
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist was a prophet.
He began his ministry on a certain day.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, something has happened.
The kingdom of heaven has faced violence.
Violent people seize the kingdom of heaven.
passages.original: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν ἡμερῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ ἕως ἄρτι ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν

passages.text: For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
passages.sermon:
All the Prophets spoke God’s message.
The Law also spoke God’s message.
They did this until John the Baptist came.
They prophesied before John.
John marks a new time.
passages.original: πάντες γὰρ οἱ προφῆται καὶ ὁ νόμος ἕως Ἰωάννου ἐπροφήτευσαν

passages.text: And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.
passages.sermon:
John the Baptist came before Jesus.
John prepared the way for the Lord.
The prophets and the Law spoke about him.
If you are willing to accept this,
John is the Elijah who was to come.
Elijah was promised to return before the Messiah.
John fulfills this role.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ θέλετε δέξασθαι αὐτός ἐστιν Ἠλίας ὁ μέλλων ἔρχεσθαι

passages.text: He who has ears, let him hear.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He gave them a message.
He said, “He who has ears, let him hear.”
He called everyone to listen carefully.
He wanted people to understand his words.
passages.original: Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω

passages.text: To what can I compare this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He wanted to describe the people living at that time.
He asked, “To what can I compare this generation?”
He answered his own question.
He said, “They are like children.”
These children sit in the marketplaces.
They call out to other children.
They say, ‘We played the flute for you.’
‘But you did not dance.’
‘We sang a sad song for you.’
‘But you did not mourn.’
passages.original: Τίνι δὲ ὁμοιώσω τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην ὁμοία ἐστὶν παιδίοις καθημένοις ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἃ προσφωνοῦντα τοῖς ἑτέροις λέγουσιν Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν Καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε Ἐθρηνήσαμεν Καὶ οὐκ ἐκόψασθε

passages.text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon!’
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John did not eat or drink like others.
People saw John.
People said, "He has a demon."
passages.original: Ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης μήτε ἐσθίων μήτε πίνων καὶ λέγουσιν Δαιμόνιον ἔχει

passages.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus came eating and drinking.
People saw Jesus eating and drinking.
They said, “Look at this man.
He is a glutton and a drunkard.
He is a friend of tax collectors.
He is a friend of sinners.”
Wisdom shows itself to be right by what it does.
passages.original: ἦλθεν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων καὶ λέγουσιν Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης τελωνῶν φίλος καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then Jesus began to denounce the cities in which most of His miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw many cities.
He did many miracles in these cities.
Most of His miracles happened there.
The people in these cities did not repent.
Jesus began to denounce these cities.
passages.original: Τότε ἤρξατο ὀνειδίζειν τὰς πόλεις ἐν αἷς ἐγένοντο αἱ πλεῖσται δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν

passages.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the cities of Chorazin and Bethsaida.
He said, “Woe to you, Chorazin.
Woe to you, Bethsaida.
I performed many miracles in you.
If I had performed these miracles in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago.
They would have shown their sorrow by wearing sackcloth and sitting in ashes.”
passages.original: Οὐαί σοι Χοραζίν οὐαί σοι Βηθσαϊδά ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγένοντο αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ μετενόησαν

passages.text: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people in the cities where He had performed many miracles.
He said these words to them.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
On the day of judgment, Tyre and Sidon will have it easier than you.
God will show more mercy to Tyre and Sidon than to you on that day.”
passages.original: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ ὑμῖν

passages.text: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
passages.sermon:
Capernaum, I speak to you now.
You will not be lifted up to heaven.
You will be brought down to Hades.
God performed miracles in you.
If God had performed these miracles in Sodom, Sodom would have remained until today.
passages.original: Καὶ σύ Καφαρναούμ μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ ἕως ᾅδου καταβήσῃ ὅτι εἰ ἐν Σοδόμοις ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν σοί ἔμεινεν ἂν μέχρι τῆς σήμερον

passages.text: But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Capernaum.
He warned them about judgment.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
On the day of judgment, Sodom will have it easier than you.”
passages.original: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι γῇ Σοδόμων ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ σοί

passages.text: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke at that time.
Jesus said, "I praise You, Father."
The Father is Lord of heaven and earth.
You, Father, hid these things from the wise.
You also hid them from the learned.
You revealed these things to little children.
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι Πάτερ Κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς ὅτι ἔκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις

passages.text: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
God saw this situation.
God was pleased with it.
God approved it.
This was well-pleasing to God.
passages.original: ναί ὁ Πατήρ ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου

passages.text: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God is the Father of Jesus.
The Father has given everything to Jesus.
Only the Father truly knows the Son.
No one else truly knows the Son.
Only the Son truly knows the Father.
No one else truly knows the Father.
The Son can choose to reveal the Father to others.
Only those whom the Son chooses can know the Father.
passages.original: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν Υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατήρ οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει εἰ μὴ ὁ Υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι

passages.text: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
He calls everyone who is weary.
He calls everyone who carries heavy burdens.
He says, "Come to Me."
He promises, "I will give you rest."
passages.original: Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus invites them to take His yoke upon themselves.
Jesus tells them to learn from Him.
Jesus says He is gentle.
Jesus says He is humble in heart.
Jesus promises they will find rest for their souls.
passages.original: ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς καὶ μάθετε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ καὶ εὑρήσετε ἀνάπαυσιν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν

passages.text: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
passages.sermon: Jesus speaks to the people.\r\nJesus says, "My yoke is easy."\r\nJesus says, "My burden is light."
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ζυγός μου χρηστὸς καὶ τὸ φορτίον μου ἐλαφρόν ἐστιν
